comparison: Both evaluate GPSite's architecture and design features (C4, C5, C33, C85-C87). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation of architectural specifications, while peer reviewers emphasize the novelty of using predicted structures and language models as key contributions. Both find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval also covers additional architectural details (C108, C113-C114, C117, C132-C137) that peer reviewers address separately.

Both address GPSite's distinguishing features (C132-C137). OpenEval validates these as part of comprehensive architectural assessment, while peer reviewers specifically highlight these as novel contributions to geometric deep learning. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and complementary.

Perfect alignment on performance claims (C6, C34-C37). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed technical validation of quantitative metrics and experimental design, while peer reviewers emphasize the convincing nature of benchmarking evidence and accept results without challenge.

Both address computational efficiency claims (C38, C68-C71). OpenEval validates timing measurements with technical specifications, while peer reviewers emphasize the practical significance for genome-scale applications. Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval covers additional technical details (C107, C112, C120, C124-C126) not explicitly mentioned by peer reviewers.

Both evaluate robustness to structure quality (C7, C44-C51). OpenEval provides detailed validation of TM-score distributions and case studies, while peer reviewers emphasize this as a key strength enabling broader applicability. Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval also addresses C41-C43 which peer reviewers discuss separately.

Perfect alignment on ablation study claims (C52-C60). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates the systematic experimental design and statistical testing, while peer reviewers praise the ablations as 'very insightful' and convincing evidence that every component is necessary.

Perfect alignment on multi-task learning benefits (C61-C64). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates quantitative improvements and provides technical assessment, while peer reviewers highlight multi-task framework as a distinguishing feature with insightful ablation results.

Perfect alignment on transfer learning and learned representations (C65-C67). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates t-SNE visualizations and quantitative results, while peer reviewers implicitly validate through overall positive assessment of method's performance and utility.

Perfect alignment on biological validation claims (C73-C74, C76-C78). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates statistical analyses and enrichment results, while peer reviewers accept biological consistency and emphasize utility for disease mechanism elucidation.

Perfect alignment on variant analysis (C79-C84). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates quantitative enrichment results while noting some interpretations are speculative, while peer reviewers emphasize utility for disease research and downstream applications.

Both address large-scale application and utility (C8, C88). OpenEval validates computational feasibility and reliability, while peer reviewers emphasize genome-scale annotations as significant advancement. Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval also covers C89 and C95 which peer reviewers address separately.

Both address utility for biological discovery (C89). OpenEval validates concordance with existing knowledge and potential for discoveries, while peer reviewers emphasize practical utility for disease mechanisms and drug design. Both are SUPPORTED.

Both address flexibility with native structures (C39-C40). OpenEval validates performance boost with native structures through quantitative data, while peer reviewers note this flexibility as an insightful ablation. Both are SUPPORTED. OpenEval also covers C41-C43 which peer reviewers address in R3.

Partial overlap on robustness advantages (C41-C43). OpenEval validates quantitative comparisons showing advantages of training on predicted structures, while peer reviewers emphasize broader applicability as key strength. Both are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval validates glucocorticoid receptor case study (C138-C140) with structural visualizations demonstrating performance despite moderate structure quality. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific case study.

OpenEval validates dataset construction methodology (C97-C104) with detailed technical assessment of quality criteria and temporal splitting. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these methodological claims.

OpenEval validates descriptions of pre-trained models (C105-C106, C109-C111) through citations and published characteristics. Peer reviewers acknowledge use of these models as contributions but do not separately evaluate these descriptive claims.
OpenEval validates training and evaluation procedures (C115-C116, C118-C119, C121) as standard and appropriate methodology. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these methodological details.

OpenEval validates data processing for large-scale analysis (C122-C123, C127-C131) with assessment of filtering criteria and quality thresholds. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these technical processing details.

OpenEval validates background context and motivation (C1, C9-C13) as supported by citations and established knowledge. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this context but do not separately evaluate these background claims.

Both address limitations of existing methods (C2-C3, C14-C23). OpenEval validates these characterizations through citations and reasonable critiques, while peer reviewers implicitly accept by acknowledging GPSite addresses these limitations. Both are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval validates context about recent advances in structure prediction and geometric deep learning (C24-C32) through appropriate citations. Peer reviewers acknowledge these advances implicitly but do not separately evaluate these contextual claims.
OpenEval validates Swiss-Prot dataset characterization (C72) through distribution data. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate this dataset characterization claim.
OpenEval validates explanation for protein-protein interaction performance (C75) as established biological knowledge. Peer reviewers do not explicitly address this explanatory claim.
OpenEval evaluates future improvement suggestions (C90-C93) as UNCERTAIN - reasonable but untested speculation. Peer reviewers do not evaluate these forward-looking claims.

OpenEval validates annotation gap context and potential applications (C94, C96) as SUPPORTED, though noting C96 is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers implicitly accept utility claims but do not separately evaluate these contextual statements.
